idiom_name: detached rows + shared column header (record set as a value)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: materialise the query into a value that owns its rows (no live cursor, no connection) and carries a column header alongside them. Expose exactly two access paths - by position and by column name - and resolve the name through the header once rather than per cell. Keep the container behaviour-free: no validation, no change tracking, no persistence; a typed projection belongs on top of it, not inside it. Bound the materialisation (page size, LIMIT, or streaming into chunks) because the whole set lives in memory, and close/free the source cursor before handing the value over. Where a consumer knows the shape, generate a typed view over the same data instead of teaching it column-name strings.
code_sketch:
record_set = source.materialize(query, params)   # owns rows, cursor already closed
record_set.columns            # ["id", "email", ...]
for row in record_set.rows:   # row["email"] or row[1]
    consume(row)
# typed layer on top: rows.map(OrderRow.from_row)
pitfalls: Handing over a live cursor (or an object still holding the connection) instead of a materialised set: consumers then fail on closed cursors or keep transactions open.
Losing the header so consumers address columns positionally; a changed SELECT list then silently mis-maps fields.
Letting the container accumulate domain behaviour until it becomes an untyped domain model.

Wrong move: Treat a pandas DataFrame or ADO.NET DataSet as the domain model -> generic columns cannot enforce business invariants or behavior -> instead map stable projections to typed domain records.
Wrong move: Materialise an unbounded query into a DataTable or Arrow Table -> memory and serialization costs grow with row count -> instead page the query or consume Arrow RecordBatch/cursor streams.
Wrong move: Expose a generic DataSet directly as a cross-service contract -> polymorphic schema and incidental columns burden non-.NET clients -> instead publish a versioned DTO or explicit schema.
